Its custom parser for bracketed IPv6 literals does not fully validate the IPv6 grammar, allowing invalid trailing text in an authority to be silently discarded. This can lead to a malformed, attacker-controlled host being normalized into a different, valid IPv6 destination, such as a local or private IPv6 target. This could allow an attacker to bypass URL allowlists or network-based access controls, potentially enabling unauthorized access to internal services, cloud metadata endpoints, or other network resources. This issue affects Red Hat products that bundle fast-uri as part of their Node.js dependencies.
